newsitem.title: USA: Iowa racetrack sale decision delayed for studies.
newsitem.headline: Iowa racetrack sale decision delayed for studies.

text.p: Polk County, Iowa, supervisors have delayed for a short period a decision on whether to sell a highly profitable government-owned race track and casino in Altoona, a county spokesman said Tuesday.

The Prairie Meadows Race Track has been appraised at $160 million and Polk County supervisors received a $200 million offer to purchase the facility after announcing its value last month, spokesman Phil Roeder said.

That offer prompted the board to request a reworking of an economic impact statement expected at the end of May and an advisory opinion from the state appeals board on the possible effect of receiving a profit on the sale twice the size of the county's annual budget, Roeder said.

Iowa law limits the fund balance that local boards may retain and supervisors cannot find a similar situation to determine how the state would view the windfall a sale would generate for Polk County, Roeder said.

Polk County supervisors had planned to decide as early as Tuesday whether they would sell the now lucrative Prairie Meadows, which had been on the verge of bankruptcy until the installation of slot machines in 1995 sparked a massive turnaround.
"I would surmise that definitely within a month that the board is going to address the issue of whether or not to put the facility on the market," Roeder said.
Polk County had sold $26.5 million of gaming revenue bonds in 1995 and $38.8 million of tax-exempt general obligation bonds in 1993 for Prairie Meadows.
The facility has 1,100 slot machines and is considering the addition of 400 more in 1998.
Projected revenues for 1997 are $123.5 million. If it continues with 1,100 slot machines, appraisers set projected revenues at $127.25 million in 1998, rising to $143.2 million in 2002.

The addition of 400 slot machines would raise projected revenues to $142.3 million in 1998 and $159.99 million in 2002, according to the appraisal report prepared by Hospitality Real Estate Counselors of Thornton, Colo., and Urban Systems Inc. of New Orleans.
